newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat turning color ahead of average.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat turning color ahead of average.

text.p: Kansas winter wheat was ripening and turning color ahead of average during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.

Wheat condition declined slightly and was rated eight percent excellent, 52 good, 28 fair, nine poor and three very poor. That compared with last week's rating of 13 percent excellent, 53 good, 23 fair, eight poor and three very poor.
Eighty-five percent of the wheat was turning color, ahead of 74 percent last year and the five-year average of 76 percent.
The report said wheat harvest was "just under way" in southern counties of Kansas.
Sorghum was 85 percent planted, ahead of 80 percent last year and the average of 65 percent. Soybeans were 95 percent seeded, ahead of 78 last year the average of 66 percent.

Corn condition also improved and was rated 15 percent excellent, 65 good, 18 fair, two poor and nil very poor. That compared to the previous week's rating of 14 percent excellent, 65 good, 18 fair, two poor and three very poor.
Pasture condition was rated nine percent excellent, 67 good, 20 fair and four percent poor.
